analysis.title: GS Consumer | Morning Trading Update (US)
key_insights: US equities are choppy pre-market (SPX futures +10 bps, NDX +45 bps, RTY -30 bps) with focus on AI ahead of NVDA's post-close EPS (stock +1% pre-market, 8% implied move).

An interim US chip export rule now requires data center operators in Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil to obtain a government license before exporting AI chips. Kioxia, Advantest, SoftBank, Hynix, Samsung and Taiwan Semi closed down 2-5%, with BABA -3% and BIDU -1% pre-market.
WTI is +45 bps at $86.10 and the UST 10-year is -1 bp at 5.12%. Today's calendar has retail sales, Fed speakers Waller, Hammack and Williams, the NKE investor day, and HD and DIS earnings.

HD (-1% pre-market) reported a small sales beat that was expected, with some pushback on the narrowing of the EPS guide. 3Q EPS was $3.86 vs consensus $3.84 on a 150 bps top-line beat, and comps were +2.2% vs consensus +1.7%.
AS (+1%) beat, raised the FY guide again and added a $1B buyback. The desk notes bar and positioning remain high. 2027 operating margin guide sits at the low end of the historical algorithm.
VIK (unch) missed 3Q EPS ($1.11 vs consensus $1.27) on low river levels in Europe, but 2027 commentary was reassuring (68% booked at +8% y/y prices).
DIS reported a solid beat across segments and reaffirmed the FY27 outlook. Q4 adj. EPS was $1.77 vs $1.67 consensus on revenue of $25.95B vs $25.16B consensus.

NKE hosts an investor day at 11:30 EST. Focus is the five-year financial algorithm and the timing and magnitude of the revenue and earnings recovery after the FY27 reset (FY27 revenue guided down high-single-digit).
Scott Feiler discusses increased shorting in staples and expects the retail earnings prints this week to be solid.
Leah Jordan upgrades UNFI to Buy from Neutral, citing EBITDA growth from natural/organic exposure, network optimization and the food-at-home inflation backdrop, with entry at 5.7x NTM EV/EBITDA.
Jon Keypour raises his AEO 3Q26 comp estimate by 90bps to +5.6% on better intraquarter sales and resilient foot traffic, and trims GRGD US sales growth by 200bps to +38.0%.
Lizzie Dove maintains Buy on ARMK and lowers her PT to $68, viewing 2027 guidance as conservative.
Leah Jordan reiterates Buy on TSN with a $70 PT after the stock closed up 8.7% on solid F4Q results and better-than-expected FY27 guidance.

Ben Snider forecasts the S&P 500 up 17% to 8,700 by year-end 2027, with EPS growth slowing to 18% from ~30% in 2026 and leadership shifting from AI infrastructure to monetization/adoption beneficiaries.

The GS Housing Activity Scale rose 2% sequentially for the week of November 8 but is down 14% y/y and 33% below the long-term average. The mortgage rate fell 7bps to 7.11%. Susan Maklari highlights IBP, MTH and DHI.
Street actions: JPMorgan downgrades TSN and assumes KMB at neutral, Bernstein downgrades PEP, Cowen names KO a 2027 top pick.

Buy maintained and PT lowered modestly on higher incentive comp and interest expense. 2027 guidance viewed as conservative with a multi-year runway for positive estimate revisions.
Improving beef trends should more than offset a softer chicken backdrop, with strength in value-added products.

earnings_insights: HD 3Q reported 11/17: EPS $3.86 vs consensus $3.84 on a 150 bps top-line beat. Comps +2.2% vs consensus +1.7%. Operating margins in line, gross margin a touch below. FY revenue guide raised to +4.5%, the top end of the prior range, with the EPS guide moved to the middle of the prior range.

AS 3Q reported 11/17: EPS $0.42 vs consensus $0.35, EBITDA 11% above consensus, revenue about 100 bps above. FY EPS guide raised to $1.32-$1.35 from $1.27-$1.30, revenue growth guide +25-26% vs consensus +25%. 2027 revenue growth guided to the mid-point of the long-term algorithm and operating margin to the low end of the +30-70 bps algorithm.
VIK 3Q reported 11/17: EPS $1.11 vs consensus $1.27, EBITDA an 8% miss, revenue missed by 1%. 2027 bookings 68% booked at +8% y/y prices vs +10% as of last quarter.

DIS Q4 reported 11/17: adj. EPS $1.77 vs consensus $1.67, revenue $25.95B vs $25.16B, segment operating income $4.97B vs $4.91B. Entertainment $1.33B vs $1.27B, Experiences $2.25B vs $2.20B, Sports $1.39B vs $1.40B. Free cash flow $4.84B vs $4.39B, cash from operations $6.76B vs $7.27B. Q1 segment operating income guide ~$5.4B vs $5.24B consensus. FY27 adj. EPS growth guided double-digit ex-53rd week vs +8.5% consensus.

ARMK 4Q26 reported: missed slightly on higher incentive comp. 2027 guidance below GS expectations, with organic revenue growth implying a continuation of FY26 trends (+9.5%) and Nexus revenue accelerating to +$500mn in FY27. $1bn buyback authorized.
TSN F4Q reported: solid results and better-than-expected FY27 guidance, with the stock closing up 8.7%.
AEO 3Q26 preview: GS comp estimate +5.6% (raised 90bps). GRGD 3Q26 preview: GS US sales growth estimate +38.0%, adj. diluted EPS estimate $0.94.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Yields are roughly flat pre-market at a high level.
Rates moved off their recent peak, supporting a 2% sequential rise in the GS Housing Activity Scale.
Housing activity remains depressed despite the sequential gain.
Positive but moderating returns, with EPS growth slowing to 18% from ~30% in 2026.
Forward P/E fell 19% in 2026 and is near its 10-year average.

NKE revenue is guided down high-single-digit in FY27, with Sportswear, Jordan and Greater China actions expected to pressure results into FY28.
Consumer softness in Hong Kong and Shanghai was cited by DIS management.
S&P 500 earnings are 25% above trend and the 2028+ outlook is highly uncertain.
VIK faces low European river levels that have pressured results.

Shorting in staples has increased of late.
AS bar and positioning remain high, and the market question is whether the $1B buyback is enough given the long positioning.
